_comment: First entry in the NT8 ground-truth trade corpus (plan phase 4.2).
Captured from a LIVE NT8 Strategy Analyzer run through the MCP bridge on
2026-09-04, saved with NT8's OWN field names and its OWN timestamp format so
that `scripts/parity/trade_set_parity.py::normalise_trades` is exercised
against the real payload rather than a schema someone guessed. The alias
table in that module was written before this capture and this file is what
confirms it: marketPosition / entryPrice / exitPrice / profitCurrency /
exitName are the real keys, and the timestamps are ET-NAIVE.
WHY BollingerCrossOver, a stock NT8 sample, and not one of this repo's bots:
none of this repo's C# strategies are deployed to NT8 (checked 2026-09-04 --
the Strategies directory has 27 files and contains no ICTFVGCISDBot and none
of the the_strat bots). Getting them there needs a sync + recompile, and a
recompile wipes every static singleton in a live NT8 that is currently
running an armed RiskGuard across 109 accounts. That is the user's call, not
a step to take while building a harness.
So this fixture proves the PLUMBING, not parity. It is a real NT8 trade set
in the real format, which is what the harness needs to be tested against.
A real parity measurement additionally needs a matched pair of strategies
and the globals below to be correct.
READ effectiveGlobals BEFORE USING THIS FOR ANYTHING NUMERIC.
GlobalMergePolicy was MergeBackAdjusted, so every price here is on a
back-adjusted continuous series. The frozen profile in
scripts/parity/backtest_profile.json requires MergeNonBackAdjusted; this
capture predates that change being made. profileHash is null because this
run did not go through the profile path at all.
knownIssuesWithThisCapture: totalCommission is 0 -- IncludeCommission was not set on this run, so these figures are not comparable to an account statement.

Every exit is 'Close position' or 'Exit on session close': this sample strategy is always-in-market and reverses, so there are no Stop Loss or Profit Target exits to compare exit-reason parity against. A corpus entry with bracket exits is still needed.

The bridge IGNORED a strategy name it could not resolve. A prior call in the same session requested '@SampleMACrossOver' (leading @) and the bridge ran '_McpTestBot' -- whatever was already loaded in the reused SA window -- returning totalTrades: 0 as though the requested strategy simply had not traded. ALWAYS check that the returned summary's name= matches what was asked for. Filed against nt8-mcp-bridge.
